title: Ranker profile orchestration: slice-aware FP8/INT8 calibration, perturbation tests, and automated gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a repeatable, slice-aware workflow to produce FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles for the production ranker model that preserves ranking quality (NDCG@10, MRR) across customer traffic segments. Current ad-hoc calibration runs show non-uniform quality regressions for low-frequency queries and long-context items. Goal: produce orchestration and automation that 1) runs calibration sweeps per data slice, 2) executes perturbation/seed sensitivity tests, 3) computes statistically rigorous pass/fail gating, and 4) auto-promotes profiles when gates pass. This ticket covers design, experiments, automation scripts, and rollout gating for runtime-2.4.0.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible pipeline that produces FP8 and INT8 profiles per slice from a single calibration job definition
NDCG@10 and MRR deltas <= 0.5% (relative) on overall benchmark and <=1.0% on all slices compared to FP32 baseline
Statistical significance computed via bootstrap with 95% CI; gates defined and enforced by automation
Integration tests that run on staging cluster and a smoke job on dedicated-dev before promotion
Docs and runbook describing failure modes and rollback steps
plan: Define canonical slice list (head queries, tail queries, long-doc, short-doc, zero-click) and sampling strategy
Implement calibration job template that accepts slice selector, quant target (FP8/INT8), and random seeds
Run systematic perturbation matrix: seeds x batch sizes x KV-cache present/absent
Measure NDCG@1/5/10, MRR, recall@k and compute bootstrap CIs; store results to perf-db
Add gating logic: fail if any slice has negative delta beyond threshold with p<0.05
Wire automated promotion pipeline: on pass, create profile artifact, tag runtime release candidate, and trigger canary rollout
Document runbook, create dashboard widgets for real-time comparison
experiments: Dataset: internal 'rank-benchmark-v3' (200k query groups), stratified into 6 slices
Calibration sweep: FP8 symmetric, FP8 asymmetric, INT8 per-channel calibrations
Perturbations: 5 random seeds, batch sizes 1/8/32, KV-cache on/off
Sample sizes: 10 bootstrap resamples of 20k query groups each to estimate CI
Metric evaluation: NDCG@1/5/10 and MRR calculated per-query-group; store per-slice deltas
findings_summary: Preliminary runs show FP8 asymmetric with per-channel scaling yields best overall parity to FP32: median NDCG@10 delta +0.02% (within noise). INT8 runs produced larger variance on tail queries: median NDCG@10 delta -0.8% with 95% CI [-1.3%, -0.4%] in tail slice when KV-cache disabled. Seed sensitivity was low for FP8 (stddev 0.1% across seeds) but higher for INT8 (stddev 0.35%). Batch-size interactions impacted INT8 most when batch>8. Based on thresholds, FP8 profile candidates pass gating for all slices; INT8 requires further per-layer clipping and a follow-up asymmetric calibration method.
decisions: Primary shipping target: FP8 asymmetric per-channel profile for runtime-2.4.0
INT8 kept as experimental channel; do not auto-promote until additional clipping/activation range caps are implemented
Add explicit KV-cache test in pipeline — profiles must be validated with cache enabled and disabled before promotion
Gating thresholds: overall relative NDCG@10 delta <=0.5%; per-slice <=1.0% with p>0.05 (bootstrap)
Use 10k-20k effective query groups per slice for stable CI estimates
risks_mitigation: Risk: INT8 tail regressions could impact customers on low-frequency queries. Mitigation: hold INT8 behind a canary rollout to internal tenants and increase logging of rank shifts
Risk: Calibration non-determinism across hardware. Mitigation: pin kernel selection in staging and verify hardware-specific kernel consistency
Risk: Overfitting calibration to benchmark. Mitigation: reserve a blind holdout slice from live telemetry for final validation
Risk: Automation bug promotes broken profile. Mitigation: require manual approval for first two promotions and add auto-rollback on runtime regression alarms
